//: The typecheck used for VERIFICATION. Identical to tsconfig.json except that it
does not include Next.js's generated type files.
*** WHY THIS FILE EXISTS ***
On 2026-09-26 `npx tsc --noEmit` reported only errors in
.next/dev/types/validator.ts -- TS1109, TS1434, TS1005, TS1128 -- and nothing
else, across the whole project. That looked like a clean result with some
generated-file noise to filter out, and it was filtered out, repeatedly.
It was not a clean result. Those are SYNTAX errors, and when a program has
parse errors tsc emits syntactic diagnostics and skips semantic checking
entirely. So every type error in src/ was invisible. Proven by appending
`const x: number = "not a number";` to a source file: tsc reported nothing.
Moving the generated file aside surfaced both that canary AND four real
pre-existing errors in citations.ts.
A generated dev-server artefact could therefore switch off the project's type
safety, silently, and the failure looked exactly like success.
`.next` is a build output. Verification does not need it: the route types it
contains are checked by `next build`, which is where a route-type error
belongs. So verification reads the source tree and nothing else.
`npm run test:typecheck-live` asserts this is still working, by requiring that
a deliberate error IS reported. A typecheck that cannot fail is not a check.
